conviction_note: Near non-result. State Street already put the quarter in the market on 2026-09-14 (fees tracking 13-14%, NII at the top of 14-15%, Q3 stable against Q2), consensus sits on that guide, and the peers that reported on 10-13 (JPM, Citi) confirm the mechanics without adding a number. The small positive (NII leverage to higher-for-longer rates) and the small negative (AFS losses running through CET1 at a Category I bank, which may trim buybacks) roughly offset. The name has sold its beats (5 of 7 prints down; Q2 2026 beat and raise -0.5%), so p_up sits at 51 on a 4.0% absolute move. impact_sum +0.2 and impact_scaled +0.08 agree in sign and are both near zero.
bar: Q3 2026 EPS $3.63 (Zacks, via Globe and Mail https://www.theglobeandmail.com/investing/markets/stocks/STT/pressreleases/6216957/higher-nii-fee-income-growth-likely-to-aid-state-streets-q3-earnings/) to $3.68 (AlphaStreet, 13 analysts, range $3.59-3.89, https://news.alphastreet.com/state-street-q3-2026-earnings-preview-october-14-street-expects-3-68-eps/amp/; GuruFocus $3.68, https://www.gurufocus.com/news/9120022/state-street-stt-set-to-report-q3-earnings-amid-mixed-valuation-signals). Revenue about $4.04B across sources, which matches the company's own 2026-09-14 framing of Q3 as stable against Q2's $4,048M (https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/state-street-at-barclays-conference-growth-ai-and-margin-gains-93CH-4900063). The bar is sourced to a company guide plus agreeing estimates, so no cap applies. print_vs_bar_pct is on revenue: a small beat (+1%) because the company said servicing and management fees ran better than modelled, and Q3 average equity levels were above Q2.
positioning_check: Short interest about 1.8% of float, about 2.0 days to cover (Equibles, about 2026-08-19, https://equibles.com/stocks/stt/short-interest; carried from the sweep row). Not crowded, so there is no squeeze mechanism against the small negative. 25-delta skew -0.36 vol points (balanced), put/call OI 0.79, event-implied move 4.67%. The stock is -6.8% over 20 sessions and -11.2% from its 52-week high, against an S&P 500 near highs (S&P 7,765 on 2026-10-08), and is down about 10% from $191.89 on 2026-09-08 despite the 09-14 guide raise. Some caution is already in the price.

findings.finding: At Barclays on 2026-09-14 the CFO said 2026 fee revenue is tracking 13-14% growth (above the July guide of 12-13%) and NII at the upper end of 14-15%. He said Q3 fees, NII and expenses are stable against Q2, servicing and management fees are running better than modelled, and markets (FX) are moderating.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (2026-07-16) beat ($3.65 vs $3.32) and raised fee guide from 7-9% to 12-13% and NII from 8-10% to 14-15%; stock -0.5% on the day (baseline). 5 of 7 prints since 2025-01 were down.
findings.why_not_priced: It is largely priced: it has been public for a month and consensus ($3.63-3.68 EPS, $4.04B revenue) sits exactly on 'stable vs Q2'. What is left is the formal print of the raised range and a Q4 outlook. If the market had extrapolated the raise, the stock would not be about 10% below its 09-08 level with a balanced skew.
findings.independence: Citi's Q3 2026 release (2026-10-13) shows Securities Services revenue +4% QoQ and +13% YoY on AUC/A +16% YoY: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000831001/000110465926115323/c-ex99d1.htm. This is filed separately below as the peer read.

findings.finding: Rates moved to higher-for-longer during and after Q3: the 10-year reached about 5.2-5.35%, the highest since 2002, and Fed minutes show most policymakers expect another hike. State Street is asset-sensitive (+/-50bp is +/-3-5bp of NIM per the Q2 call). JPMorgan raised its NII outlook on 2026-10-13, so a firmer Q4/2027 NII outlook is plausible.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: NII guide raised from 8-10% to 14-15% in July 2026; stock -0.5% (the raise came with a fee raise, so the effect is not separable). No clean NII-only surprise in the baseline window.
findings.why_not_priced: The guide still assumes the July rate path (Fed and BoE on hold, one ECB hike), and it was set before September's long-end move and the hawkish minutes. If the market had priced a higher NII run-rate, an asset-sensitive custodian would not have lagged the S&P by about 10 points into the print. Partly priced, because the rate path is public.
findings.independence: JPMorgan raised its 2026 NII outlook on its Q3 2026 print (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/jpmorgan-profit-misses-analyst-estimates-as-jamie-dimon-warns-economic-forces-shift-under-the-surface-112446859.html, 2026-10-13). Rate levels and Fed minutes: https://komeytetteh.com/weekly/week-in-markets-october-9-2026 (2026-10-10). This is a proxy: State Street has not confirmed it, and deposit migration at higher rates cuts against it.

findings.finding: Q3 was one of the worst bond quarters in years (Bloomberg Agg about -4%, 10-year from about 4.8% on 09-01 to 5.1-5.2% by late September). As a Category I GSIB, State Street carries AFS losses through CET1, which stood at 10.8% against an about-11% target. Both peers that reported on 10-13 named AFS/OCI losses as a CET1 drag, and JPM cut its buyback to about $1B, so Q3 capital return or the Q4 buyback pace may come in light.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No capital-return surprise in the baseline window. Q2 2026 returned $631M ($400M buybacks) with CET1 up 20bp QoQ (Q2 release).
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus previews talk about NII and fees, not capital. The ~80% payout guide from 09-14 still stands publicly. If the market had priced a buyback cut, previews would carry lower share-count assumptions. The 20-day underperformance may already be partly this, which is why it is sized small.
findings.independence: Citi's Q3 2026 release names unrealized AFS losses as an offset to CET1 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000831001/000110465926115323/c-ex99d1.htm). Agg -4% in Q3 per First Citizens (https://www.firstcitizens.com/content/dam/firstcitizens/pdfs/wealth/market-outlook/2026/q3-2026-quarterly-market-review.pdf). Macro-to-company transmission: State Street's AFS size and duration for 2026 were not found (2022 10-K duration 2.6 years after a $23.6B transfer to HTM), so the CET1 hit is unquantified.

findings.finding: Citi's Q3 2026 Securities Services revenue rose 4% QoQ and 13% YoY, with AUC/A flat QoQ at $35T and FX revenue up on volumes. JPM's FICC fell 4% YoY while currency flows rose. Both read through to State Street's servicing fees as stable to up and FX as moderating, not collapsing.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Servicing-fee surprises have not been bought: Q2 2026 servicing +13% YoY on a beat, stock -0.5% (baseline).
findings.why_not_priced: It was published the session before the print, after State Street last spoke. It lands inside what the company guided on 09-14, which is why it is near zero.
findings.independence: JPM Q3 2026 call (FX client flows higher, FICC -4% YoY): https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-jpmorgan-chase-misses-q3-2026-forecasts-as-profits-stay-strong-93CH-4946956. Shares the Citi document with finding 3, but reads a different line of it.

baseline_tension: Balanced skew and a -6.8% 20-day run-up against a market near highs. My findings net to roughly zero, so they neither confirm nor fight the skew. The run-up may already hold the capital/AOCI concern and part of the rate story.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction; this name sold its Q2 beat and raise) and lesson 6 (the finding lands inside the guide): finding 1 went from +0.3 to +0.2, and p_up from 52 to 51.
